Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 49

Mass, Center of Mass, and Moment of Inertia of a Cylindrical Wedge

A solid in the first octant is cut from a quarter cylinder by the slanted plane y=z. The density grows with all three coordinates.

Problem

Let E be the solid in the first octant bounded by the cylinder x2+y2=1 and the planes y=z, x=0, and z=0. The density function is

ρ(x,y,z)=1+x+y+z.

Use exact values to find (a) the mass of E, (b) the center of mass of E, and (c) the moment of inertia of E about the z-axis.

Reading the solid

The cylinder x2+y2=1 cuts the first quadrant of the xy-plane in a quarter disk. The two planes x=0 and z=0 hold the solid against the coordinate planes. The plane y=z holds it below the slanted roof z=y.

The roof tells the height of the solid at every point of the quarter disk. Above a fixed point (x,y) with y>0, the solid runs from z=0 up to z=y. The height therefore grows with y and never exceeds the radius of the disk. This gives the three sets of bounds

0≤y≤1,0≤x≤1−y2​,0≤z≤y.

The order z, then x, then y matches this shape: the inner integral covers one vertical segment, the middle integral covers one horizontal strip, and the outer integral sweeps the quarter disk from the x-axis to the point (0,1).

Solution

Step 1. Write the mass integral

The mass is the integral of the density over the solid. With the bounds above,

M=∫01​∫01−y2​​∫0y​(1+x+y+z)dzdxdy.

Step 2. Integrate in z

The inner integral runs over a segment of height y. At fixed x and y,

∫0y​(1+x+y+z)dz=(1+x+y)y+2y2​=y+xy+23​y2.

The constant term 1+x+y gives the rectangle y(1+x+y), and the term z gives the triangle y2/2.

Step 3. Integrate in x

The upper limit is s=1−y2​, so the middle integral is

∫0s​(y+xy+23​y2)dx=ys+21​ys2+23​y2s.

Replace each even power of s by a power of 1−y2. The mass then reduces to three radial integrals over 0≤y≤1:

M=∫01​ysdy+21​∫01​y(1−y2)dy+23​∫01​y2sdy.

Step 4. Evaluate the radial integrals

The substitution y=sint, with dy=costdt and s=cost, turns each integral into a trigonometric integral on 0≤t≤π/2. For example,

∫01​y21−y2​dy=∫0π/2​sin2tcos2tdt=16π​.

The integrals that the moments need are listed below. Every entry follows the same substitution.

IntegralValueIntegralValue
∫01​ysdy1/3∫01​ys2dy1/4
∫01​y2sdyπ/16∫01​y2s2dy2/15
∫01​y3sdy2/15∫01​ys3dy1/5

Here s=1−y2​. These six integrals cover every radial integral on the page.

Step 5. The mass

Insert the three values:

M=31​+81​+323π​=2411​+323π​=9644+9π​≈0.752858.

The middle term is 21​⋅41​=81​.

Step 6. The moment about the yz-plane

The first moment of mass about the plane x=0 weights each point by its distance x from that plane:

Myz​=∫01​∫0s​∫0y​x(1+x+y+z)dzdxdy.

The inner integral gives xy+x2y+23​xy2. The integral in x then gives

21​ys2+31​ys3+43​y2s2.
Myz​=21​⋅41​+31​⋅51​+43​⋅152​=81​+151​+101​=247​≈0.291667.

Step 7. The moment about the xz-plane

Repeat with the weight y. The inner integral gives y2+xy2+23​y3, and the integral in x gives

y2s+21​y2s2+23​y3s.
Mxz​=16π​+21​⋅152​+23​⋅152​=16π​+154​≈0.463016.

Step 8. The moment about the xy-plane

Repeat with the weight z. The inner integral gives 21​y2+21​xy2+65​y3, and the integral in x gives

21​y2s+41​y2s2+65​y3s.
Mxy​=21​⋅16π​+41​⋅152​+65​⋅152​=32π​+301​+91​=32π​+9013​≈0.242619.

Step 9. The center of mass

Divide each first moment by the mass:

xˉ=MMyz​​=11/24+3π/327/24​=44+9π28​≈0.387.
yˉ​=MMxz​​=11/24+3π/32π/16+4/15​=5(44+9π)30π+128​≈0.615.
zˉ=MMxy​​=11/24+3π/32π/32+13/90​=30(44+9π)90π+416​≈0.322.

All three coordinates lie in the interval (0,1), as they must, because the solid sits inside the unit cube. The centroid lies nearer the y-axis than the x-axis, because the solid is tallest at y=1.

Step 10. The moment of inertia about the z-axis

The squared distance from a point to the z-axis is x2+y2, so

Iz​=∭E​(x2+y2)(1+x+y+z)dV.

Expanding the product gives eight monomial terms. Each one is an elementary integral of the same three-step form, and the script evaluates all eight:

(x2+y2)(1+x+y+z)=x2+y2+x3+x2y+x2z+xy2+y3+y2z.
Term∭E​(⋅)dVTerm∭E​(⋅)dV
x21/15x2yπ/96
y22/15x2zπ/192
x31/24xy21/24
y3π/32y2zπ/64

The squares collect to 51​, the cubes and mixed products collect to 121​, and the four terms with π collect to 16π​:

Iz​=51​+121​+16π​=6017​+16π​≈0.479683.

Answer

(a) The mass is

M=2411​+323π​=9644+9π​≈0.753.

(b) The center of mass is

(xˉ,yˉ​,zˉ)=(44+9π28​, 5(44+9π)30π+128​, 30(44+9π)90π+416​)≈(0.387, 0.615, 0.322).

(c) The moment of inertia about the z-axis is

Iz​=6017​+16π​≈0.480.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
EThe solid that the six boundary surfaces enclose.
ρ(x,y,z)Mass density at the point (x,y,z), in mass per unit volume.
dVVolume element, equal to dzdxdy in the order used here.
First octantThe region where x≥0, y≥0, and z≥0.
sShorthand for 1−y2​, the radius of the quarter disk at height y.
MMass of the solid, the integral of ρ over E.
Myz​,Mxz​,Mxy​First moments of mass about the planes x=0, y=0, and z=0.
xˉ,yˉ​,zˉCoordinates of the center of mass, for example xˉ=Myz​/M.
Iz​Moment of inertia about the z-axis, the integral of ρ times the squared distance x2+y2.
y=sintSubstitution for the radial integrals, with dy=costdt and 0≤t≤π/2.

Verification

  • part1_step1.py integrates in the order z, x, y with SymPy, prints the inner integrals, the six radial integrals, the four first moments, the three centroid coordinates, and the eight monomial integrals of Iz​.
  • part1_step2.py recomputes the mass, the three first moments, and Iz​ by nested mpmath quadrature and by Monte Carlo sampling of 4,000,000 points in the unit cube. Both checks agree with the exact values to the printed digits.
  • part1_figure1.py draws the solid, the quarter-disk base, the slanted roof, and the cylinder wall.
